lessen.titel: Take a unit or two of chaff so you are not left without strategic pieces
lessen.tekst: An army of only damage dealers and casters leaves you little to do, and your opponent gets to dictate the tempo. A unit or two of chaff lets you disrupt his plans and enables your powerful units.
lessen.waarom: He found that armies made only of death stars, dragons, damage dealers and casters left him with little to do on the table. Chaff lets you interfere with the opponent's plans and enables your powerful units, and it often costs under 100 points. He also finds it makes the game more strategic, so you feel more like a general.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He cautions against spending too many points on chaff: these units support the fighting block, which still has to do the work.

bronnen.citaat: you get to stuff with your opponent's plans

extraCitaten.citaat: these units are costing you under 100 points

bronnen.citaat: one or two pieces tends to be pretty good.

lessen.titel: Use speed bumps to pull enemy units out of position
lessen.tekst: A speed bump redirects enemy units by getting in the way, so they charge it or cannot get around it. It is there to die, but to die while achieving something.
lessen.waarom: It all comes down to wasting your opponent's time: getting in the way forces him into decisions he did not expect or want to make. Part of a list's win condition can be that this unit moves an enemy out of position so it cannot perform at its peak. Redirecting is difficult, but he thinks mastering it makes you a top tier player.
lessen.voorbeeld: He put a Great Eagle in front of Grail Knights that threatened his Waywatchers and Wild Riders. The knights had to charge and kill the eagle, overran in the direction he chose, and his Wild Riders could later charge them without being countercharged and win that flank.

bronnen.citaat: their main function is to redirect things and move enemy units out of position
Sometimes its job is simply to stand in the way.
They're very good at redirecting charges.

lessen.titel: Decoys with kill potential draw resources away from your real threats
lessen.tekst: Fast, dangerous chaff that threatens backline units like artillery or light cavalry cannot be ignored. While your opponent spends shooting and units on it, he is not dealing with your bigger threats.
lessen.waarom: Decoys are fast and dangerous, so if left alone they threaten backline units such as artillery and light cavalry, or become a flanking force that turns a key combat. Dealing with them costs the opponent resources and buys time for your win condition. He likes them most because they do not just take up space: they threaten a space and force a response.
lessen.voorbeeld: An enemy Helblaster Volley Gun shooting a 95 point Mangler Squig is not shooting your big unit of Boar Boyz. He names the Mangler Squig as his favourite decoy and a Hell Pit as an expensive version that works the same way.

bronnen.citaat: Your opponent has to pour resources into dealing with them.

extraCitaten.citaat: point mangler, which buys time for your win potential

bronnen.citaat: you have to kill it or be killed by it.

lessen.titel: Use cheap units as early deployment drops
lessen.tekst: Without chaff you end up putting your key units down early, before your opponent. Cheap drops force him to commit his units first, so you can react and place your win conditions in the matchups you want.
lessen.waarom: If every unit in your list must perform to win, you end up dropping your key pieces first, and that alone shapes the game. When the opponent places his big flanking unit before your counter unit, he has committed to a flank and you can react. Scouts also gain intel during deployment.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wood Elf Beast Packs, a handler and two beasts for about 30 points, are in his view the best scout unit in the game. Giant Rats at 30 points without a handler do the same, and in marching column they become a speed bump.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He says extra cheap drops can be wasted on armies that really want to go first and therefore prefer as few deployment drops as possible.

bronnen.citaat: If you don't have chaff in deployment, you're often dropping your key pieces down early
You can deploy these units early to give yourself more drops than your opponent.
It allows you to waste drops

lessen.titel: Chaff must be fast or mobile
lessen.tekst: Chaff has to get into position ahead of the enemy, so it needs high movement or mobility such as fly, skirmish or reserve move. For a speed bump the speaker wants fly or movement seven as a minimum.
lessen.waarom: Chaff is about getting into position ahead of the opponent; too slow and it cannot get in the way or into the right spot to flee in the direction you want. He separates speed (high movement) from mobility (skirmish, fly, reserve move), which lets chaff use every corner of the board.
lessen.voorbeeld: His checklist: under 100 points and movement seven or more, with fly, skirmish or reserve move as bonuses. For a speed bump he wants fly and movement seven as a minimum.

bronnen.citaat: needs to be fast because it's about getting them in position ahead of your opponent

extraCitaten.citaat: The speed and the mobility of the speed bump is very very important

lessen.titel: Keep chaff cheap, roughly under 100 points
lessen.tekst: Chaff is likely to die, so it should be cheap; the speaker uses about 100 points as the threshold. A unit above that has to give a good return to be worth it.
lessen.waarom: Chaff has to go into dangerous parts of the board, so it is likely to die and the return shrinks as it gets more expensive. He credits an early Wood Elf guide by AJ of the Rank and Flank podcast for the under 100 points threshold and thinks it still holds.
lessen.voorbeeld: For elves, a unit of seven Dryads with a Nymph at about 120 points can still be chaff, because chaff is defined by what it is trying to do.
lessen.wanneerNiet: Some armies can go over 100 points, but then the unit has to give a good return.

generally cheap is under 100 points for the unit.

lessen.titel: The best chaff covers several roles, but give each unit a specific job
lessen.tekst: Chaff that can fulfil multiple roles is the best kind: Giant Rats can be a cheap scout drop and a speed bump, and a Great Eagle can redirect and still kill a war machine. Each chaff unit should still go in the list for a specific role.
lessen.waarom: Chaff shines when it can fulfil more than one role, but each unit should still go in the list as the time waster for a specific role.
lessen.voorbeeld: Giant Rats are a scout just by being cheap and placed early, and a speed bump because they are fast and their formation lets you control how units contact them. The Great Eagle is there to redirect with its close order, yet with three or four attacks, a stomp, strength four and weapon skill five it can also kill a war machine.

lessen.titel: Mangler Squigs make a strong decoy on a flank
lessen.tekst: With a 3D6 random move the opponent has to respect an 11 to 12 inch threat in any direction. Placed on a flank opposite something like Chaos Knights, they make the knights hold back and delay their push into your backline.
lessen.waarom: He sees Mangler Squigs as chaff and the perfect decoy: a 3D6 random move, strength six impact hits, killing blow, stomps and random attacks give huge damage potential. The threat makes the opponent change how he moves, and with toughness five and four wounds they may win the combat if they get to hit back.
lessen.voorbeeld: Rangers were shooting him while pushing down his right flank. He moved his Manglers into range until one could hit them; over two or three combats they killed the whole unit without losing a Mangler, and soaked up the arrows in the meantime.
lessen.wanneerNiet: The random move can also come up short, as low as four inches, and they have to wheel.

lessen.titel: Use light chariots as decoys and artillery hunters
lessen.tekst: A Goblin Wolf Chariot is fast and its impact hits threaten lightly armoured units such as Outriders and artillery. Pushed forward, it cannot be ignored, which buys time for your main units.
lessen.waarom: Light chariots are good decoys and also good speed bumps. They cannot be ignored because their impact hits can kill Outriders, which opponents like to protect. A Goblin Wolf Chariot is very fast with swift stride, and artillery has little armour, so its impact hits are a real threat.
lessen.voorbeeld: In his Nomadic Waaagh list one chariot pushed forward to pressure Outriders and bait the Demigryph Knights, buying his Wyvern a turn. Another stood beside his Boar Boyz to shape a Griffon's charge; when the Griffon charged the Boar Boyz instead, the chariot roamed free and smashed a mortar in one turn.

bronnen.citaat: Wolf chariots are great artillery hunters.

lessen.titel: A decoy wins either way: killed late or left free
lessen.tekst: The job of a decoy is not to die but to make your opponent choose between wasting time killing it and letting it run free to do its job.
lessen.waarom: If you do not deal with a decoy it has something to do, so it is not just there to die. He notes that opponents often decide to go and kill it anyway.

bronnen.citaat: The job is to make your opponent decide whether to waste time killing it
Their sole role isn't to die

extraCitaten.citaat: your opponent's not going to let their great cannon die.

lessen.titel: A speed bump must be close or open order, not skirmishers
lessen.tekst: A charging unit has to align to the front of a close or open order speed bump, so when it wins it overruns in a direction you chose, for example away from the flank of your main unit. Skirmishers cannot steer the post-combat movement this way; the speaker thinks a Great Eagle is the best unit for it.
lessen.waarom: A speed bump takes a hit, dies and shapes the post combat movement. With close or open order the charger has to align to its front, so when it wins it overruns in a direction that protects your other units, and you may countercharge the unit that got sucked in (Chaff video). Against a close order Great Eagle the charger either takes a restraint test and stays put for the turn, or overruns in the direction you chose (Flanks video).
lessen.voorbeeld: Skin Wolves charged his open order Goblin Wolf Riders, killed them and overran in a direction that protected the flank of his Boar Boyz. He adds that a Boar Chariot wheeled a little further could then have countercharged the Skin Wolves (Chaff video).
lessen.wanneerNiet: Skirmishers can still pull a unit where you want if it is frenzied or you are its only possible charge target, but they cannot shape the post combat move this way.

bronnen.citaat: being a speed bump is non-negotiable. It cannot be a skirmish unit
It has close order, so the opponent has to align to it.
most importantly they're non skirmishers.

lessen.titel: When frenzy baiting, be the only unit they can redirect to
lessen.tekst: A fast speed bump can sit at the edge of a frenzied unit's charge range, take the charge, flee and rally. Make sure there is nothing else for the enemy to redirect into, or the bait is wasted.
lessen.waarom: A speed bump with swift stride is his main frenzy bait: it can sit at the very edge of a frenzied unit's charge range, make it charge, then flee and try to rally. If the enemy can redirect into something else after you flee, the whole move was a waste of time.
lessen.voorbeeld: He calls a Razorgor a very good speed bump and decoy for this.

lessen.titel: Think of the board in thirds and aim to win two of them
lessen.tekst: Plan your game as left flank, centre and right flank. You do not need to win all three: winning two thirds of the board generally wins the game.
lessen.waarom: It is the overarching principle: deployment ties the flanks and the centre together, and what you do afterwards decides whether you roll into the middle or the backline and own space. You do not need to win all three thirds.
lessen.voorbeeld: Two thirds can be the centre and one flank, or both flanks, after which you overwhelm the centre with a bigger flanking force than the enemy has left there.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He frames this as a principle for balanced games and notes that a massive list disparity can allow one army to win all three thirds.

lessen.titel: Most armies hold the centre, win the flanks, then overwhelm the centre
lessen.tekst: About 80 percent of armies rely on a heavy anvil in the middle. Winning a flank is usually not enough on its own; the point is to free your flank units to turn on the centre later.
lessen.waarom: Faster units sit on the flanks, so the action starts there early, while the centre becomes a standoff about who holds longest. If your flank units do not get unlocked you cannot win the centre. Flank matchups are rarely one sided, so you often sacrifice something to win one.
lessen.voorbeeld: Against Alex's Beastmen his block of Black Orcs with a Shaman and battle standard, about 700 points, held the centre. His stacked right flank won, then his Squig Hoppers and Wolf Riders charged into the central combat and turned it.
lessen.wanneerNiet: With Wood Elves, which he also plays, he thinks you win by winning the flanks and creating space, because winning the centre alone is very hard.

lessen.titel: On a flank you either kill things or waste time
lessen.tekst: Put units that can hit hard on the flank you mean to win, and use chaff to delay the enemy on the other one. Both are valid ways to play a flank.
lessen.waarom: You need units that can hit things to destroy the enemy on one flank, and chaff to delay the enemy on the other. He calls that split the key to getting the most out of flank units.
lessen.voorbeeld: His skirmishing characters, frenzied Boar Boyz and Squig Hoppers did the killing on his right, while Goblin Wolf Riders on his left used feigned flight to draw a charge and get away.

lessen.titel: Do not just park heavy cavalry on a flank and charge the closest target
lessen.tekst: A five-wide unit of knights on the flank charging whatever comes closest is a misconception. Pick your fights in deployment and support your hammer with chaff such as wolf riders.
lessen.waarom: Once your hammer is on the flank it needs support from units like wolf riders. Simply placing a great flank unit such as Wild Riders at the edge of your deployment and sending it off does not work, and neither does parking a Heavy Chariot on a flank just because it does nothing in the middle.

bronnen.citaat: It's not that simple. You need to pick your fights through deployment

lessen.titel: Judge a flank by who benefited, not by units lost
lessen.tekst: The speaker lost more points on one flank but still counts it as won, because his chaff bought the time he needed elsewhere. What happened on the flank and who gained from it matters more than the kill count.
lessen.waarom: Delaying the enemy on one flank can buy the time you need to win elsewhere. His Wolf Riders baited a charge and escaped, which bought a turn, then beat an infantry unit and came into the middle while the enemy Preyton was busy with his Boar Chariot.
lessen.voorbeeld: He lost the Boar Chariot and the Doom Diver on that flank, about 190 points, but it took his opponent longer than planned, which gave him time to win the right flank and the middle.

lessen.titel: Combat infantry is too slow to win flanks
lessen.tekst: A good flank unit has speed, damage and durability. Infantry at movement four or five cannot compete with light or heavy cavalry out there; its strength is holding space in the centre.
lessen.waarom: Infantry's power is holding space and combat resolution. Its big drawback is speed: movement four, or five for elves and rats, cannot compete with light cavalry outmanoeuvring you or heavy cavalry picking its charge.
lessen.voorbeeld: In his game his Night Goblins stood on the left flank but faced the centre, because that is where they would be needed.

bronnen.citaat: I don't think you can really win flanks with infantry

extraCitaten.citaat: And their big disadvantage is they are slow.

lessen.titel: Give your hammers the speed to get the charge
lessen.tekst: Hammers are rarely effective when they are not charging. Look for high movement (seven or more, or six with swift stride), swift stride and countercharge so your hammer gets the charge it wants.
lessen.waarom: Charging is vital for winning combats on the flank, so he counts heavy cavalry as fast enough from about movement six with swift stride (Flanks video). Hammers are rarely effective when not charging; swift stride, countercharge and skirmish give redundancy, so you still get the matchup you want whatever happens on the table (Infantry video).
lessen.voorbeeld: Demigryph Knights have movement seven and swift stride, a 16 inch charge range, and countercharge lets them still charge back when out of position (Infantry video). Glade Riders with movement nine and reserve move use their speed to distract rather than to deal damage (Flanks video).
lessen.wanneerNiet: Speed is about what the unit does with it, not only the raw number (Flanks video).

extraCitaten.citaat: So speed needs to be thought of more than just a raw number

lessen.titel: Keep heavy cavalry and other hammers on the flanks, not in the centre
lessen.tekst: In the middle of the board hammers tend to get shot by everything. On the flanks you can use terrain to block line of sight and screen them with chaff until they can strike.
lessen.waarom: On the flanks a hammer can manoeuvre around terrain, use it to block line of sight from shooters, and be covered by screening skirmishers or chaff. In the middle, because of the terrain rule for the centre of the board, hammers tend to get blown up straight away. From the flanks they can later turn to the centre or get into the backline.
lessen.voorbeeld: He approves of his opponent placing a Tuskgor Chariot on the extreme flank.

lessen.titel: Hammers need some durability because they will be targeted
lessen.tekst: Your opponent wants to kill your hammers first, so they need some redundancy: toughness four or more and at least a 3+ save, a 2+ preferred on heavy cavalry. Then they survive long enough to deal their damage.
lessen.waarom: Hammers win games, so the opponent targets them and they are often the first thing shot. If a hammer does not strike first in combat it is wasted; durability gives it redundancy to take a hit and still deal its damage.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wild Riders have no durability and get smashed by toughness four, 2+ save, multi wound Demigryph Knights if they fail to kill in the first round (Infantry video). Orc Boar Boyz with toughness four, a 5+ save and a 6+ ward will not go down to light shooting (Flanks video).

bronnen.citaat: You need some redundancy of toughness four or above a three up at least save
the reason they need durability is because your opponent wants to kill your hammers

lessen.titel: Put a mobile wizard on the flank, away from the dispel bubble
lessen.tekst: Opponents usually keep their wizard in the middle for a big dispel range. A reserve-move or flying caster on the flank can move out of that range, cast, and drop back to safety.
lessen.waarom: If the enemy pulls his own wizard out to the side to deal with yours, you have already won part of the mind game, and your caster is probably the more manoeuvrable one.
lessen.voorbeeld: A Renegade Crowns outcast wizard with Dark Magic cast his hex and enchantment, then used reserve move to drop out of dispel range, cast Doombolt and go back to safety. He mentions Pegasus riders, with versions in Dark Elves and Empire, and the Wood Elf Warhawk and reserve move Spellweaver.

lessen.titel: Skirmishing combat characters excel on the flanks
lessen.tekst: A skirmishing combat character can pick off targets or join your flank unit in a combat. Its 360 degree line of sight for charging gives it the flexibility to choose its fight.
lessen.waarom: With skirmish and a high charge distance it can pick things off and join combats you can compound, with the choice to commit alongside your flank unit or pick another target. He says such characters sway the course of the battle for about 250 to 300 points.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Orc War Boss on boar fought next to his Boar Boyz on the flank. He also uses a Great Stag version at about 280 to 300 points.

lessen.titel: Screen hammers with cheap chaff that clears itself out of the way
lessen.tekst: Expendable chaff or a skirmishing screen gives cover to the unit behind it. When it needs to get out of the way, it charges something and sacrifices itself, and your hammer goes in.
lessen.waarom: A great flank unit placed at the edge of deployment and sent off does not work; the flank needs investment, and a screen protects your hammer until it picks its target.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wood Elf Beast Packs live on the flank and cover Wild Riders; once the screen gets out of the way, the Wild Riders pick their target and charge. Chaos Warhounds are another example of expendable chaff.

bronnen.citaat: When they need to get out of the way, they just charge something
A cheap disposable unit in front of your real damage dealer

lessen.titel: Sacrificing a flank is fine if you gain from it
lessen.tekst: Double down on the flank you want to win and use chaff to waste time on the one you expect to lose. The speaker accepts forfeiting a flank, but only when it buys something elsewhere.
lessen.waarom: You win a flank by doubling down on it and using chaff to waste time on the flank you expect to lose (Flanks video). A Heavy Chariot parked on a flank only because it does nothing in the middle sacrifices that flank for no gain.
lessen.voorbeeld: Against Empire he effectively gave up his left flank after a deployment mistake, but won his right flank heavily and broke through the middle; the game was a draw. Against Bretonnia an Eagle and Wildwood Rangers held one flank almost alone and drew fire that helped his main units break through (Deploy video).

willingly sacrificing a third is also a pretty strong strategy.

lessen.titel: Terror is a powerful tool on the flanks
lessen.tekst: On a flank the enemy is away from his general and close to the board edge, so a unit that flees from terror takes turns to get back, if it returns at all. A cheap character with a faction item that grants terror can do this too.
lessen.waarom: Making an opponent flee is a huge deal: even if the unit rallies, it takes many turns to get back to the centre. Monsters already suit the flanks with high toughness, mobility, stomps and impact hits, so one that causes terror is even better.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Arachnarok Spider caused terror in a Leadership 9 Renegade Crowns sellsword unit; it fled, lost its warband bonus and ran off the board, 160 points gone, and he turned into the middle. He also mentions a Wood Elf banner that gives fear, which lets Wild Riders cause terror.

bronnen.citaat: Terror is such a powerful tool on the flanks

lessen.titel: Once a flank is won, turn into the centre or the backline
lessen.tekst: Winning a flank opens up space. Use it to push into the backline against war machines and wizards, or turn into the centre and flank charge the units holding it.
lessen.waarom: Your flank units should support the rest of the board, while the units in the centre do the dirty work of holding it.
lessen.voorbeeld: After his Arachnarok Spider won its flank, it turned and drove straight through the middle of the board.

bronnen.citaat: And when you win the flank, you open up space for you to play in.

lessen.titel: A hammer first of all has to deal damage
lessen.tekst: Hitting power is the most important part of a hammer: many attacks, high strength, armour piercing, stomps or impact hits. Durability and mobility come after that.
lessen.waarom: The hammer is the unit that breaks the enemy while the anvil holds it in place. Whatever the unit type, dealing damage is the first and most important job.

lessen.titel: Send each hammer into the matchup it wins
lessen.tekst: Wild Riders do well into infantry but come out second best against heavily armoured heavy cavalry. A hammer that underperforms may simply be in the wrong matchup, which you set up at deployment and with chaff.
lessen.waarom: He sees matchups as about 80 percent of the game. They are decided at deployment or by enabling your hammers with chaff, screens and buffs.
lessen.voorbeeld: Wild Riders kill enough infantry without being hit back, but against Demigryph Knights with a 2+ save, toughness four and multiple wounds they get smashed if they do not kill in the first round.

bronnen.citaat: You might just be sending it into the wrong matchup

lessen.titel: Behemoths make good hammers on the flanks
lessen.tekst: Stomps give them reliable damage, and terror means a unit that loses to them is more likely to flee instead of falling back in good order. Most behemoths can stomp their way out of a bad engagement.
lessen.waarom: Behemoths can wreck both infantry and heavy cavalry through high strength and AP2 thunder stomps, and they often have five or more high strength attacks with good AP.
lessen.voorbeeld: A Giant Spawn of Chaos rolling a six on its stomps will cook Wild Riders and even hurt Demigryph Knights with strength six AP2 hits.

extraCitaten.citaat: mainly because of their high strength and their thunder stomps

lessen.titel: Use heavy chariots as support pieces, not as your main hammer
lessen.tekst: Put something in front that holds and falls back in good order, then countercharge with the chariot to get its impact hits in. The speaker would not recommend heavy chariots to new players.
lessen.waarom: When they connect, heavy chariots are devastating through their impact hits. But the first charge bonus is easily wasted, they are easy to kill with only four wounds and hard to get into position, and impact hits can spike but are never certain.
lessen.voorbeeld: D6+1 impact hits at strength five AP2 can wreck a unit of infantry.

lessen.titel: Infantry can hold and kill if it keeps armour piercing while parrying
lessen.tekst: A hybrid hammer has some static combat resolution and durability but also high quality attacks, so it kills models when it is charged. It needs weapons that still give armour piercing when parrying, such as the speaker describes for Chaos Warriors and Stormvermin.
lessen.waarom: He finds units that are only immovable boring; a hybrid brings static combat resolution and durability but kills models when it hits back, so the opponent is invited to come for the points and can be punished. Being able to parry and still hit with armour piercing is a massive deal.
lessen.voorbeeld: Chaos Warriors with ensorcelled weapons are strength four AP1 with a 3+ save in combat. Stormvermin with halberds can parry for a 3+ save and hit back at AP1, or use the halberds for AP2 on the charge.

lessen.titel: Run Black Orcs with great weapons, two ranks deep

lessen.tekst: Use a control mage to disrupt enemy movement, including spells that reduce movement. He considers even Elementalism's minus-one-movement signature useful for interfering with carefully judged charge and missile ranges.
lessen.waarom: In his view, movement is the source of the game's advantages. Good players operate as close as possible to the relevant range boundaries, making movement buffs or debuffs valuable.

lessen.titel: Consider Necromancy to attack enemy leadership
lessen.tekst: Consider Necromancy's leadership debuffs as a control tool. He particularly values the minus-two leadership effect for its potential to make critical leadership tests fail.
lessen.waarom: He regards failing leadership tests as the next most important lever after movement: the effect may seem irrelevant until a decisive failure occurs.

lessen.tekst: He considers a High Priest on a Necrolith Bone Dragon an ideal carrier for control magic because it can choose Illusion or Necromancy. Consider an Illusion setup with movement-disrupting and blocking spells, or Necromancy with Spirit Leech and other debuffs.

lessen.titel: Use control spells to obstruct movement and charging lanes
lessen.tekst: Look for control magic that blocks line of sight or creates dangerous or difficult terrain to interfere with enemy charges and movement. He regards forcing the opponent to take the low charge roll through terrain as an underused tool.
lessen.waarom: He recalls the disruption Wood Elves could cause by blocking movement and charging lanes with Pillar of Fire and Tree Singing when those options were more effective.
lessen.voorbeeld: He tried to bridge a gap between terrain pieces with Crystal Column to block the magic-missile firing lane to his Terrorgheist, but his opponent dispelled it. In another game, he wanted Crystal Column in a gap to delay a charge and gain another turn of objective points.

lessen.titel: Use impassable terrain to create safe lanes for advancing
lessen.tekst: Use impassable terrain to create a lane where a unit can attack, advance after winning combat and escape an enemy charge on the following turn.
lessen.waarom: He values being able to keep moving forward after winning a combat while the terrain protects the unit from a counterattack.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Mortis Engine fitted into a narrow pocket beside the Herdstone, where he found its unusual base size a major advantage.

lessen.titel: Use impassable terrain to restrict enemy frontage
lessen.tekst: Try to hem advancing enemy units in against impassable terrain and limit the frontage they can use.
lessen.waarom: He says restricting frontage makes it awkward for the enemy to move and limits their options.
lessen.voorbeeld: He consciously tried to limit the frontage of the opposing Dragon Ogres as they advanced across the board.
lessen.wanneerNiet: He warns that terrain used to block line of sight or maintain control of a position can also hem in your own units.

lessen.titel: Attack skirmishers where terrain obstructs forming ranks
lessen.tekst: Look for a charge into one side of a large skirmishing unit where impassable terrain prevents models from reaching the rear ranks when forming up. He recommends exploiting this vulnerability to remove skirmishers.
lessen.waarom: He identifies coherency as a weakness of large skirmishing units. In his game, moving around the impassable terrain used more distance than some models could cover when forming ranks.
lessen.voorbeeld: His Mortis Engine charged beside the Herdstone, and about half the opposing skirmishing unit died because it could not form up around the terrain.
lessen.wanneerNiet: His event's judge required the models to form ranks and fit through the gap rather than scatter around the terrain; that ruling determined which models could reach their positions.

lessen.titel: Use impassable terrain to shorten enemy retreats
lessen.tekst: Try to force enemies to flee towards impassable terrain so they cannot escape as far and are easier to catch. He suggests terrain-creating spells can make this easier to arrange.
lessen.waarom: He argues that even if the fleeing unit is allowed to snake around the obstacle, moving sideways costs movement rather than increasing its distance from pursuers.
